summary:
Kendall answers a question that raw climate maps cannot: is this change a real long-term trend, or just weather noise?

We built a free, in-browser explorer that analyses 304 consecutive months (June 2000 – September 2025) of NASA Earth observations—GPM IMERG precipitation, GLDAS Noah land-surface data, and MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis—across 12 variables on a global 2.5° grid. For every grid cell, Kendall removes the seasonal cycle, estimates the rate of change using Sen's slope, and tests statistical significance via the Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall test to correct for autocorrelation, alongside False Discovery Rate (FDR) control.

Clicking any point or drawing custom regions returns a plain-language verdict (significant trend, trending but not yet significant, or no trend), 95% confidence intervals, a "detectability clock", and automated warnings when sensor transitions (such as the 2014 TRMM-to-GPM break) might distort trends. Narrated case files (Amazon, Sahel, Tibet, Canada) teach users to interpret trends honestly, preventing false alarms and missed signals for farmers, planners, journalists, and students.
details:
What it does

Kendall is an interactive, zero-backend planetary exploration system that answers a fundamental question for any location on Earth: "Has this climate variable truly experienced a statistically significant shift over the past 25 years, or are we observing natural weather variability?"

Covering 25.33 continuous years (304 consecutive months: June 2000 – September 2025) across 10,368 global grid cells (2.5° × 2.5° resolution), Kendall analyzes 12 NASA satellite and reanalysis variables:

  • Precipitation: GPM IMERG Final V07B satellite observations and GLDAS Noah 2.1 land surface flux.
  • Surface & Atmosphere: GLDAS 2m air temperature, MERRA-2 skin/surface temperature, surface pressure, and precipitable water vapor.
  • Hydrology & Cryosphere: Topsoil moisture (0–10 cm), evapotranspiration, snow water equivalent (SWE), and snow depth.
  • Aerosols & Dynamics: MERRA-2 550 nm aerosol optical depth (AOD) and 10m surface wind speed.

Users can click any coordinate on an interactive 3D WebGL globe / 2D flat map or draw a custom polygon region. Kendall instantly computes:

  1. 25-Year Deseasonalized Anomaly Trajectories: Time series with 12-month rolling means and Theil-Sen median slopes.
  2. Plain-Language Statistical Verdicts:
    • Significant Trend (p<0.05p < 0.05p<0.05): Confirmed multi-decadal shift after accounting for temporal persistence and multiple testing.
    • Trending, Not Yet Significant: Directional slope detected, but current observation length cannot mathematically rule out random chance.
    • No Trend: Historical variability remains within natural bounds.
  3. The Detectability Clock: Calculates the exact minimum years of continuous observation needed before a regional trend of that magnitude emerges above background climate noise.
  4. 2014 Satellite Era Break Guard: Automatically warns users when precipitation trends reverse direction across the 2014 TRMM-to-GPM constellation upgrade.
  5. Multiple-Testing "Looks" Counter: Tracks analytical query combinations and dynamically calculates cumulative false discovery inflation (1−(1−0.05)m1 - (1 - 0.05)^m1−(1−0.05)m) to guard against p-hacking.
  6. Multi-Variable Cross-Check Lineup: Side-by-side consistency check across complementary NASA observations (e.g., rainfall decline vs. soil moisture deficit vs. evapotranspiration).

How it works

  1. Data Ingest: Automated Python pipelines fetch monthly NetCDF4/HDF5 granules from NASA GES DISC and GMAO via Earthdata authentication (GPM IMERG, GLDAS Noah 2.1, MERRA-2).
  2. Conservative Spatial Regridding: Native satellite grids (0.1° GPM, 0.25° GLDAS, 0.5°×0.625° MERRA-2) are regridded onto a uniform 2.5° × 2.5° equal-angle grid using area-weighted conservative averaging, standardizing physical units (e.g., kg⋅m−2⋅s−1→mm/month\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} \to \text{mm/month}kg⋅m−2⋅s−1→mm/month, K→∘C\text{K} \to ^\circ\text{C}K→∘C).
  3. Deseasonalization (Historical Baseline): Each month's observation is evaluated against its 25-year calendar-month climatology (e.g., July 2024 vs. all historical Julys from 2000 to 2025), stripping regular annual cycles.
  4. Theil-Sen Robust Median Estimator: Calculates the median rate of change across all pairwise temporal differences, completely resisting single-event outliers such as 100-year floods or acute droughts.
  5. Hamed-Rao Autocorrelation Correction + FDR Control: Natural weather exhibits temporal persistence (wet months follow wet months). Kendall calculates the effective sample size (n∗n^*n∗) using the Hamed-Rao variance inflation factor to eliminate false alarms, paired with Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) control across all 10,368 grid cells.
  6. Domain-Aware Binary Web Packaging: Anomalies are quantized to signed 16-bit integers and compressed into binary cubes with JSON metadata. The entire 25.33-year global payload across all 12 variables compiles to just 38.93 MB, with quantization error bounded below 0.0270.0270.027.
  7. Client-Side Statistical Engine: The complete statistical engine is implemented natively in client-side JavaScript, enabling instant, real-time recalculations for any custom polygon or season with zero round-trips to a server.

Benefits

  • Separates Reality from Weather Noise: Eliminates false trend alarms by telling decision-makers when observations are simply not yet statistically significant.
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Operates 100% in-browser with zero installation, zero server infrastructure, no database setup, and no API keys. It runs instantly on any laptop, tablet, or smartphone.
  • Full Scientific Transparency: Every verdict exposes raw p-values, corrected Hamed-Rao p-values, 95% confidence intervals, and explicit physical caveats.
  • Zero Operational Cost: Being entirely client-side, the application can be hosted indefinitely on static platforms (e.g., GitHub Pages) with zero cloud infrastructure expense.

Intended impact

  • Agricultural Planners & Water Authorities: Distinguish temporary multi-year dry spells from genuine long-term desiccation trends before making permanent infrastructure commitments.
  • Climate Journalists & Fact-Checkers: Instantly cross-verify public claims (e.g., regional greening or drying) against 25 years of calibrated NASA Earth Science data.
  • Educators & Students: Foster critical scientific and statistical literacy by demonstrating how autocorrelation, satellite sensor transitions, and repeated testing alter conclusions.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, or software used

  • Programming Languages: Python 3.11, Modern ES6+ JavaScript, Semantic HTML5, CSS3.
  • Scientific Computing & Data Pipeline: xarray, netCDF4, h5py, NumPy, SciPy, pandas, pymannkendall, PyYAML.
  • In-Browser Visualization & Mapping: MapLibre GL JS 5 (3D WebGL globe & 2D planar projection morphing), Apache ECharts 5 (time series & confidence bands), D3 7, TopoJSON Client.
  • Development & Packaging: Conda package management on macOS (Apple Silicon), Python static HTTP server. No external cloud compute was required.

How it is creative

  1. Teaching When NOT to Believe a Trend: Unlike conventional dashboards that display a linear regression line over any data, Kendall actively protects users from deception through the Detectability Clock, the 2014 Sensor Transition Guard, and the Multiple-Testing Looks Counter.
  2. In-Browser Scientific Computing: Instead of relying on static pre-baked maps or slow server-side GIS processing, Kendall runs the entire non-parametric statistical suite directly in the client's browser, calculating area-weighted trends over user-drawn polygons on the fly.
  3. Seamless Projection Morphing: Users can smoothly transition between an interactive orthographic 3D WebGL globe and an equirectangular flat map without losing pin placement, telemetry state, or temporal playhead position.

Factors considered

  • Observational Limitations vs. Reanalysis Realities: I explicitly distinguish direct satellite retrievals (GPM IMERG) from assimilation models (GLDAS, MERRA-2) and highlight where independent NASA products diverge (e.g., Tibetan Plateau warming rates).
  • Satellite Constellation Shifts: NASA’s 2014 transition from TRMM to GPM altered precipitation detection thresholds. I built explicit automated guards to prevent sensor upgrades from being misclassified as climate shifts.
  • Polar Quality Masking: Polar latitudes (>60∘> 60^\circ>60∘) are masked from statistical significance calculations to prevent satellite retrieval artifacts over sea ice and ice sheets from distorting results.
  • Bandwidth & Digital Inclusion: Compressing multi-decadal planetary grids into a 38.93 MB payload ensures researchers and students in bandwidth-constrained regions can access the entire 25.33-year archive.
